name: Abbot Daniel's pilgrimage to the Holy Land
traveler: Daniel, abbot of a monastery near Chernigov
summary: A Rus' abbot travels by way of Constantinople and the Greek islands to crusader Jerusalem, stays sixteen months, rides with King Baldwin to Galilee and sets a lamp at the Holy Sepulchre for all the land of Rus. His account is the earliest Russian travel book.

stops.note: Sets out from his monastery in the land of Chernigov.
Down the Dnieper and across the Black Sea to Tsargrad.
Through the Greek islands, visiting the tomb of St John.
Sixteen months in the holy city, with a guide who knows every place.
With King Baldwin's escort to the Sea of Galilee.
At Easter he sets a lamp on the Holy Sepulchre for all the princes of Rus.
Home, where he writes it all down.

informs.note: The Holy Land seen by a Russian pilgrim
